section.title: Introduction
section.simpara: This document sets out our vision for the project: what it is, why it matters, and how we intend to make it succeed.

section.title: Purpose
section.simpara: Formal methods and model-based approaches to software development gained industrial traction in the 1960s–1980s through close collaboration between academia and industries operating under extreme safety and reliability demands — the earliest being defence, aerospace, and nuclear power. Their use broadened during the 1990s–2000s to other life-critical (railways, automotive, medical devices) and high-stakes domains (hardware design, finance). They are now gradually entering mainstream software engineering, finding applications in cloud computing, cybersecurity, and blockchain.
Papillon Journey seizes this momentum and tackles three persistent barriers to broader adoption:

listitem.simpara: Limited exposure. The historical confinement of these approaches to high-assurance niches has unintentionally reinforced the misconception that they are irrelevant to the daily concerns of most software professionals. Demonstrating their power through large-scale, open-source initiatives in web, mobile, and game development will help dispel this view. That is why Papillon Journey will be cross-platform — playable directly in a web browser or via native applications on smartphones, tablets, and PCs, including handheld gaming PCs.

Fragmented tooling. Companies favour tools that integrate smoothly into existing workflows. Those supporting formal methods — narrowly specialised and rarely interoperable — often fail to do so. Chrysal Studio, the research subproject of Papillon Journey, will explore and prototype an integrated engineering environment to change that. We will start building with the patchwork of disjointed tools available today, transitioning progressively to Chrysal Studio, until it can fully sustain both itself and the game.

Inverted pedagogy. Children learn to add and multiply long before they ever hear of ring theory — and only if they choose to. Yet formal modelling is typically taught the other way around: heavy on theory, light on practice, and illustrated with simplistic toy examples that bear little resemblance to the challenges encountered in industry. Fusing the experience of a JRPG (for example, Final Fantasy) with that of a training platform (such as Coursera) without breaking immersion is no small feat. One thing is certain, though: learners will spend most of their time practising. The very nature of JRPGs will steer us away from the pitfall of inverted pedagogy.

section.simpara: For Papillon Journey to be a living example of what it teaches, it must be libre: open for study, contribution, and adaptation. We require only that derivatives remain libre and clearly distinguished from the official project through distinct branding and separate trademarks.
Formal modelling deserves wider visibility through a transparent, participatory, and engaging real-world use case accessible across various devices.

section.title: Stakeholders and value propositions
section.simpara: Value propositions evolve alongside the people they serve. As their goals, challenges, and expectations shift, some facets are reinvented and others phased out. Even so, certain core needs persist — and these are what keep a project relevant over time. Below, we outline those that matter most to our stakeholders and map them to value propositions. For a deeper dive, see papj-doc-03.

section.title: Video game players
section.simpara:
Training is future-oriented: the time and effort invested in it aim to unlock later payoffs — a job, promotion, career pivot, or proficiency. There is no such thing as training for the sake of it. The appeal of gaming, on the other hand, is precisely a break from that logic. Players expect games to provide a brief window in their day through which they can throw out all future concerns and fully enjoy the present moment. An experience that fails to honour this misses the whole point.
This is why Papillon Journey will be, above all, fun.

It will be a play-anywhere-anytime game by design. The web version will render 2D isometric visuals with vector-based, hand-drawn art that looks great and performs beautifully on everything from smartphones to desktops. Where hardware permits, native editions on Windows, Linux, Android, iOS/iPadOS, and HarmonyOS will elevate the experience with enhanced 2.5D graphics, richer lighting, and added depth. Progress will synchronise across all platforms, so players can switch between devices.

Using in-game systems such as courier services or trading posts, players will be able to share resources, discoveries, and hard-won strategies whenever it suits them, without needing to be online at the same time.
Certain locations and NPCs will also offer mini-games in which they can compete live. These multiplayer features will feel like a part of the world rather than something bolted on.

As the player base expands, Papillon Journey will pursue partnerships with renowned game franchises to create crossover content. Such scope-limited collaborations will reconnect players with characters and stories they already love while they learn formal engineering. For partner studios, this will be a distinctive opportunity to associate their franchises with education, skill-building, and positive social impact.

section.title: Software engineering learners
section.simpara: The initial training of a software engineer reaches a satisfying end once they have the skills to turn software ideas into working, maintainable systems. Teamwork is one of them, as most systems are built through collaborative effort. Continuing education then becomes a pursuit of mastery and specialisation.
Papillon Journey will support both stages of the learners’ journey in two mutually reinforcing ways:

listitem.simpara: The fundamentals will be woven into the gameplay, so learners build skills through playful practice of product and project management, UX design, specification, development, verification, and validation. As they advance the story, the levelling up of their characters will mirror their own progress, with the climactic endgame putting their skills to the ultimate test.

For learners eager to apply lessons learnt in-game to real-world scenarios, the project’s libre codebase will serve as an expansive playground for deeper mastery. The comprehensive and high-quality documentation will empower them to study, contribute to, and adapt it with confidence. Dedicated community channels will foster support, collaboration, and knowledge sharing, ensuring no one navigates this journey alone.

section.simpara: We never truly know something until we teach it to someone else. Papillon Journey will provide a mod development framework that enables players to upskill one another. It will facilitate the creation of custom downloadable content (DLC) that transforms visuals, reshapes the soundscape, alters game mechanics, introduces new quests, tells new stories, and covers additional training topics. By officially embracing modding, we will motivate learners to dive into the source code and practise formal engineering in earnest.

Mods featured in-game will be selected through a transparent, fair, and community-driven peer-review process in which learners actively participate. To maintain a clear legal boundary, they will be indexed from third-party repositories rather than hosted on the project’s infrastructure. The process will filter out insecure or IP-infringing content, protecting the Papillon Journey trademark from association with harmful or unauthorised material. Any that erroneously slipped through will be de-indexed upon report, and every mod update will have to undergo re-evaluation before being re-indexed. Beyond risk mitigation, this collaborative effort will sharpen learners’ awareness of the cross-cutting concerns of security, legal compliance, and quality assurance.

section.title: Software engineering educators
section.simpara: Software engineering is a vast discipline whose frontier keeps expanding — rapidly. Without guidance, newcomers can easily feel lost or remain trapped at the surface, chasing one trend after another while missing both the broader picture and the deeper foundations. The educator’s role is to help them navigate the field, meeting them where they are and guiding them towards where they want or need to go.

Effective navigation relies on reference points: at sea, a lighthouse; ashore, a landmark. For educators, the equivalent is a canonical work — a book, a research paper, or a project — that learners can steer by. Formal engineering does not lack reference texts; what is missing is an industrial-scale project designed to be taught from, so educators no longer have to rely on toy examples alone.

Papillon Journey will be that real-world project. Its engineering lifecycle will be anchored in industry standards, starting with ISO/IEC/IEEE 12207, while its documentation will be deliberately written as teaching material for classrooms and self-study.

Teaching is never one-size-fits-all. Some learners respond more readily to play than to conventional instruction. For them, a gamified approach may unlock understanding that lectures and homework projects do not.

Educators at partner organisations will co-create with us adventures for players and prospective learners that showcase their expertise and the distinctive character of their programmes. Their development will follow a dedicated partnership process, giving partners an official presence in the game through a route more prestigious than community mods. This will offer partners a valuable path to audiences who may not encounter them through conventional outreach.

row.entry: As a player drawn to the genuine breaks from daily concerns that video games offer, I would be pleased if my play sessions also gave me valuable real-world skills. But I am not looking for educational games that sacrifice fun for instruction. I want gameplay that puts entertainment first, so that I can fully enjoy the present moment.

As a player, I sometimes buy multiple versions of my favourite video games for home, handheld, and mobile devices, or rely on cloud gaming to enjoy them wherever and whenever I have time and feel like playing. But progress remains fragmented across devices, operating systems, digital storefronts, and cloud gaming services. I want a game playable on any screen, with progress that follows me, so that I can always pick up where I left off.

As a player who enjoys cooperating with others, but whose schedule rarely allows live sessions, I want in-game systems that let me share resources, discoveries, and strategies whenever it suits me, so that I can stay connected and contribute to a shared adventure on my own terms.

As a player who loves both JRPGs and live competition, I would prefer not to turn to a different genre to find worthy opponents. I want competitive encounters within the world I am exploring, so that I can enjoy the thrill of competing without leaving the adventure.
